title: Spring Lake NC voters get free rides to early voting sites - ABC11 News
text:
Spring Lake NC voters get free rides to early voting sites - ABC11 Raleigh-Durham

 Free rides help Spring Lake voters amid no local early voting site 
 As early voting continues in North Carolina, some Spring Lake residents are facing an unexpected obstacle: getting to the polls. By Penelope Lopez Wednesday, October 21, 2026 10:54PM Share SPRING LAKE, N.C. (WTVD) -- As early voting continues in North Carolina, some Spring Lake residents are facing an unexpected obstacle: getting to the polls.
 With no early voting site in Spring Lake and no public transit options, residents like Deena Harrington must travel to Fayetteville to cast their ballots .
 "The polling place, surprisingly, was right around the corner from us all for Roof Street. But now, they do not have an early voting polling place in Spring Lake," said Harrington, who has called the town home for eight years.
 To help bridge the gap, a group of volunteers from The Word Church of Spring Lake, in partnership with the Liberty Delta Sigma Group, is offering free rides to voters in need. Liberty Delta Sigma is also covering the cost of gas for the effort.
 Pastor Stephan Anderson, who leads the program, says the need for rides is high. "We started last week, so they can text or call us, and we'll build up our route for the day and we make different times. But when we come pick you up, we stay here and wait, and then we bring you back home the way safely back home."
 Harrington says voting now takes more planning than before. "I actually I did call The Word Church yesterday, and was able to send an appointment."
 Pastor Anderson says the group has already helped about 40 people get to the polls. During the interview, his phone rang with yet another request for a ride. "Yeah."
 According to the Women Voters League, 91.3 million women voted in the 2024 election. Harrington is determined to make her vote count this year, too.
 For Harrington, the service is about more than just transportation.
 "I can remember as a child growing up, I've seen the civil rights movement. I've witnessed it on TV. The dogs, the firehose. And I know how important our ancestors' struggles were in making this possible."
 As Election Day approaches, volunteers hope their efforts will ensure that no one's vote is left behind for lack of a ride.
